recent_posts.title: Ceiling division and mip map sizes
recent_posts.summary: Explores ceiling division techniques for graphics programming, specifically for calculating mipmap sizes. Shows how the standard formula (n + k - 1) / k can cause overflow issues and presents an alternative (n - 1) / k + 1 that avoids this problem. Demonstrates how this optimization applies to texture block calculations in formats like BC1-BC7, where working with sizes-minus-1 throughout the pipeline eliminates bias terms and simplifies hardware implementations.

recent_posts.title: Why creators should reject the content creator label
recent_posts.summary: The term 'content creator' reflects the perspective of distribution platforms rather than creators themselves. Content is industry jargon used by those managing logistics and pipelines who treat creative work as undifferentiated material to be processed. Creators should avoid this dehumanizing self-descriptor and instead embrace more specific terms that reflect their actual craft, whether it's writing, art, music, or experimental work.

recent_posts.title: Oodle 2.9.14 and Intel 13th/14th gen CPUs
recent_posts.summary: Intel 13th and 14th gen CPUs experience hardware degradation in the clock tree circuitry, causing frequent system crashes and decompression errors in games using Unreal Engine. Oodle 2.9.14 introduces a workaround that potentially reduces these decompression errors. Despite new microcode updates from Intel, these hardware issues persist, and affected machines may require replacement to fully resolve the problems.

recent_posts.title: UNORM and SNORM to float, hardware edition
recent_posts.summary: The post explains the hardware method for converting UNORM and SNORM numerical formats to floating-point (float) values, specifically targeting the IEEE 754 binary32 format. It discusses the basic principles, special cases, and general strategy for conversion, including handling of special values and rounding steps. Techniques used include bit shifts, normalization, and rounding processes to ensure accurate results.

recent_posts.title: MRSSE
recent_posts.summary: MRSSE (Mean Relative Sum of Squared Errors) is the error metric used in the BC6H encoder for Oodle Texture to handle HDR data efficiently. The metric, designed to offer better visual results, balances linear system solving with computational efficiency and decent performance on various image tests. It was favored over other error metrics after extensive testing, particularly for its ability to manage highly saturated bright colors better than its closest alternatives.

recent_posts.title: Exact UNORM8 to float
recent_posts.summary: Converting an 8-bit UNORM format to a floating-point number in GPUs can be done by dividing the integer by 255, which ensures an exact result in float32. While D3D11.3 specifications consider precise conversion too expensive, practical experiments show that GPUs can handle it efficiently. For those seeking exact conversion without using doubles or divides, an alternative method involving geometric series and multiplications is proposed, achieving high precision with minimal computational cost.

recent_posts.title: BC7 optimal solid-color blocks
recent_posts.summary: This post explains the optimal encoding of 4×4 blocks of solid colors in BC7 texture compression. Unlike BC1, BC7 allows precise color matches due to its encoding options. The author provides a method to determine optimal color endpoints, ensuring accurate representation of 8-bit RGBA input colors using BC7 mode 5's interpolation formula.

recent_posts.title: Why those particular integer multiplies?
recent_posts.summary: The x86 instruction set has a range of unique SIMD integer multiply operations, deeply rooted in the architecture since the Pentium MMX era. The post explores the implementation and idiosyncrasies of these operations across different iterations, including MMX, SSE, SSE2, SSSE3, SSE4.1, and AVX-512. It delves into specifics of commands like PMULLW, PMULHW, PMADDWD, and others, detailing their purposes, historical context, and technical intricacies. The discussion also touches on the evolution of these operations and how Intel and AMD have adapted their multiplier designs over time.

recent_posts.title: Inserting a 0 bit in the middle of a value
recent_posts.summary: A method for inserting a 0 bit in the middle of a value, inspired by Oodle Texture's BC7 decoder, is discussed. The post details both a standard and a more optimized approach for this operation. It also includes an analogous method for removing a 0 bit from the middle of a value.

recent_posts.title: Zero or sign extend
recent_posts.summary: The post discusses dealing with bit-packed formats containing integers of varying bit widths and signedness. It highlights the awkwardness of traditional sign-extension techniques using bit-shifting and offers alternative methods that do not rely on this approach. The alternative leverages the inherent properties of two's complement representation to simplify the code and make it independent of specific integer widths.
